study type: Clinical Practice Guideline (based on systematic reviews, randomized controlled trials, and observational studies)
exposure: Local anaesthetic, blocks, oral analgesia, and conscious sedation
Concomitant insertion of a levonorgestrel intrauterine system
outcome: Complication rates (uterine perforation, fluid overload, hematometra, cervical lacerations, nausea/vomiting, uterine cramping, pain)
cohort: Women of reproductive age with abnormal uterine bleeding and benign pathology, with or without structural abnormalities.
finding: Endometrial ablation is a safe and effective minimally invasive surgical procedure and a well-established alternative to medical treatment or hysterectomy for abnormal uterine bleeding in select cases.
mod_finding: The guideline mentions considering resectoscopic techniques for endometrial ablation in patients with a history of cesarean delivery to allow direct visualization of the cavity and myometrial defect.
